hypotheses.justification: The statement is still true for every k, because the 0-component of chiMK vanishes identically unless k % 4 = 3. By definition chiMK κ m k t x = (-(corrTime ..)) • uShear β Λ m k x. Look at uShear x 0 in each case. If k % 4 = 1, uShear is ![0, ...], so its 0-component is 0. If k % 4 = 3, it is -(2π a ε cos(2π x 1/ε)), which is the active case. Otherwise uShear is 0. So when ¬(k % 4 = 3), the function y ↦ chiMK κ m k t y 0 is identically 0. Then the existing lemma ChiMKCorrector.chiMK_spaceLap_of_zero_component, which appears earlier in the same file with the hypothesis hzero : (fun y => I.chiMK κ m k t y j) = fun _ => 0, gives exactly the stated conclusion (both sides are 0). The proof is by_cases hk : k % 4 = 3. The positive case is the current proof, with hk as a local hypothesis. The negative case is: apply chiMK_spaceLap_of_zero_component with j = 0, proving hzero by funext y; simp [Ingredients.chiMK, uShear], then split on k % 4 = 1 and use hk. Nothing in the statement mentions hk, so removing it does not break elaboration.
